_comment: Exposure knowledge base. Keyed by nmap service name; fall back key 'port:NNNN'. Severity reflects the risk of the service being reachable by an unauthorised network position, not a claim that it is exploitable.

telnet.title: Telnet reachable
telnet.detail: Telnet carries credentials and session data in cleartext. Anyone able to observe the path can read the login exchange.
telnet.remediation: Disable the telnet daemon and use SSH. If a device only speaks telnet, isolate it in a management VLAN reachable solely from a jump host.

ftp.title: FTP service reachable
ftp.detail: FTP authenticates and transfers data in cleartext, so credentials are exposed to passive observers. Anonymous access is also common on older deployments.
ftp.remediation: Replace with SFTP/FTPS. If legacy FTP must stay, restrict source addresses and confirm anonymous login is disabled.

microsoft-ds.title: SMB file sharing reachable
microsoft-ds.detail: SMB exposes file shares, authentication and (historically) a large attack surface. Reachability from an untrusted segment is the precondition for most lateral-movement paths.
microsoft-ds.remediation: Block TCP 445/139 at segment boundaries, disable SMBv1, require signing, and confirm guest access is off.

netbios-ssn.title: NetBIOS session service reachable
netbios-ssn.detail: Legacy NetBIOS exposes host and workgroup information and is rarely needed on modern networks.
netbios-ssn.remediation: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP where it is not required, and filter TCP 139 at the boundary.

ms-wbt-server.title: Remote Desktop reachable
ms-wbt-server.detail: Exposed RDP is a frequent entry point for credential-stuffing and pre-auth vulnerabilities. Exposure to the internet or to untrusted internal segments increases risk materially.
ms-wbt-server.remediation: Front RDP with a VPN or an RDP gateway, enforce Network Level Authentication and account lockout, and restrict source addresses.

vnc.title: VNC remote console reachable
vnc.detail: VNC commonly ships with weak or absent authentication and offers full interactive desktop control once connected.
vnc.remediation: Tunnel VNC over SSH/VPN rather than exposing it, set a strong password, and bind it to localhost where possible.

ms-sql-s.title: Microsoft SQL Server reachable
ms-sql-s.detail: Database ports exposed beyond the application tier widen the attack surface and expose authentication to brute force.
ms-sql-s.remediation: Bind the database to the application subnet only, disable the sa account, and enable login auditing.

mysql.title: MySQL reachable
mysql.detail: A database port reachable from an untrusted segment allows credential attacks and, in misconfigured cases, unauthenticated access.
mysql.remediation: Restrict the bind address and firewall rules to application hosts; verify no account is reachable from '%'.

postgresql.title: PostgreSQL reachable
postgresql.detail: Exposed PostgreSQL invites credential attacks and, with loose pg_hba.conf rules, trusted-network access.
postgresql.remediation: Restrict listen_addresses and pg_hba.conf to application hosts, and require scram-sha-256 authentication.

mongodb.title: MongoDB reachable
mongodb.detail: MongoDB historically shipped without authentication bound to all interfaces; even now, an exposed port often means an unauthenticated database.
mongodb.remediation: Enable authorization, bind to localhost or a private interface, and restrict access at the firewall. Confirm --auth is set.

redis.title: Redis reachable
redis.detail: Redis has no authentication by default and supports commands that write files or load modules, which turns unauthenticated reachability into code execution in many setups.
redis.remediation: Bind to 127.0.0.1 or a private interface, set requirepass/ACLs, and disable or rename CONFIG, MODULE and DEBUG.

memcache.title: Memcached reachable
memcache.detail: Memcached offers no authentication and can be abused for cache poisoning or as a reflection/amplification source.
memcache.remediation: Bind to localhost/private interface, disable UDP, and firewall the port to application hosts.

elasticsearch.title: Elasticsearch reachable
elasticsearch.detail: Elasticsearch clusters are frequently found without authentication; an open API exposes every indexed document, including credentials and personal data.
elasticsearch.remediation: Enable the security features (xpack.security or OpenSearch security), bind to a private interface, and require TLS plus authentication.

http.title: Unencrypted HTTP service
http.detail: Traffic to this service, including any credentials or session cookies, can be read or modified in transit.
http.remediation: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS with HSTS once a certificate is in place; keep a plaintext listener only for the redirect.

ldap.title: LDAP reachable
ldap.detail: Plain LDAP transmits directory queries and simple-bind credentials in cleartext, and directory data aids attacker reconnaissance.
ldap.remediation: Use LDAPS/StartTLS, restrict access to domain controllers from client subnets, and disable anonymous binds.

snmp.title: SNMP reachable
snmp.detail: SNMPv1/v2c use community strings sent in cleartext, and 'public'/'private' are still common. Read access leaks full device inventory and configuration detail.
snmp.remediation: Move to SNMPv3 with authPriv, change default community strings, and permit polling only from the monitoring host.

tftp.title: TFTP reachable
tftp.detail: TFTP has no authentication and no integrity checking; it is used to push firmware and configuration to network devices.
tftp.remediation: Restrict TFTP to the provisioning VLAN and a single source host, or replace it with a signed transfer mechanism.

nfs.title: NFS export reachable
nfs.detail: NFS export lists are often readable, and exports without root_squash can allow privilege escalation from a client.
nfs.remediation: Restrict exports by host, set root_squash and no_subtree_check, and firewall port 2049 to known clients.

rpcbind.title: RPC portmapper reachable
rpcbind.detail: Portmapper enumerates registered RPC services, simplifying reconnaissance of NFS and related subsystems.
rpcbind.remediation: Firewall port 111 to clients that genuinely need it, and prefer NFSv4 which needs no portmapper.

docker.title: Docker API reachable
docker.detail: An unauthenticated Docker API grants container creation with host mounts, which is equivalent to root on the host.
docker.remediation: Never expose the Docker daemon socket over TCP without mutual TLS; use a local socket or an authorising proxy.

kubernetes.title: Kubernetes API reachable
kubernetes.detail: The API server is the control plane. Anonymous access, weak RBAC or exposed kubelets frequently lead to cluster takeover.
kubernetes.remediation: Set --anonymous-auth=false, enforce RBAC and audit logging, and restrict API access to the control network.

jenkins.title: Jenkins exposed
jenkins.detail: Jenkins executes arbitrary code as part of normal operation; unauthenticated script consoles and plugin vulnerabilities are common.
jenkins.remediation: Enable authentication and matrix-based authorisation, disable the CLI and script console, and keep plugins patched.

ipmi.title: IPMI/BMC reachable
ipmi.detail: Baseboard management controllers give out-of-band console access and have a long history of authentication bypass and default credentials.
ipmi.remediation: Keep BMCs on a dedicated management network, change default credentials, and patch firmware.

x11.title: X11 display reachable
x11.detail: An open X display can allow keystroke capture and window access without authentication.
x11.remediation: Disable TCP listening in X, or tunnel X11 over SSH with X11 forwarding.

distccd.title: distccd reachable
distccd.detail: distcc compiles supplied source remotely, which is remote code execution by design when unauthenticated.
distccd.remediation: Bind distccd to the build network only, use --allow lists, and never expose it beyond trusted hosts.

rsync.title: rsync daemon reachable
rsync.detail: rsync modules configured without auth users expose directory contents and, with 'use chroot = no', writable paths.
rsync.remediation: Set auth users and secrets file, restrict hosts allow/deny, and prefer rsync over SSH.

couchdb.title: CouchDB reachable
couchdb.detail: CouchDB's admin party mode (no admin user) allows full database control; older versions had query-server code execution.
couchdb.remediation: Create an admin user, bind to a private interface, and restrict _utils and _config from untrusted sources.

zookeeper.title: ZooKeeper reachable
zookeeper.detail: ZooKeeper has no authentication by default; znode contents often include connection strings and credentials.
zookeeper.remediation: Enable SASL authentication, use ACLs on znodes, and restrict port 2181 to cluster members.

mqtt.title: MQTT broker reachable
mqtt.detail: MQTT brokers frequently allow anonymous publish/subscribe, exposing device telemetry and allowing command injection into IoT fleets.
mqtt.remediation: Require username/password or client certificates, disable anonymous access, and use TLS on 8883.
